controls.title: Building Security Risk Management Systems
controls.overview: A system to manage security risks as a company, with roles and responsibilities defined, has been established.
controls.status_description: The roles and responsibilities of people and/or a system to manage security risks are regularly reviewed.
recommended_actions: Build a security risk management system
Plan for sufficient budget and personnel for security measures and business execution. Evaluate the plan at management meetings, etc., and secure necessary budget and personnel.
Understand the overall picture of the organization's security measures and establish an organization that maintains, improves, and supervises security levels.
Manage security risks like business risks, on par with other risks (e.g., compliance, financial, reputational risks).
Clarify the relationship between the (IT) security risk management system and other risk management systems.
Establish a suitable communications framework with relevant authorities and other security entities.
Define roles and responsibilities for security risk management system
Define roles and responsibilities in developing, implementing, and assessing the organization's cybersecurity strategy.
Divide work appropriately between work handled by your organization and outsourced work.
After clarifying the roles and responsibilities of each party, inform each party to fulfill their roles and responsibilities.
Separate conflicting duties and authorities from the perspective of segregation of duties.
Where the organization uses business partners, such as contractors or vendors, clearly define the extent of roles and responsibilities regarding information security.
Establish a communication framework for cybersecurity that involves all departments across the organization, including executive management, business units, and security personnel.
Identify and manage security risks when initiating and managing a project within the organization, regardless of the project's nature.
Regularly review the security risk management system, roles and responsibilities

Regularly review and, if necessary, improve the security risk management framework system based on audit results, changes in laws and regulations, and requirements from related parties (customers, local communities, shareholders, etc.).
Regularly review budget and personnel required for security measures and business execution.
controls.insufficient_measures_risks: Inappropriate or sub-optimal allocation of management resources (people, things, and money) may result in waste of these resources and hinder efficient execution of security response and system. Failure to align with other risk management systems (i.e. risk management systems other than IT security/cyber risk) within the organization can lead to inconsistency in risk management and across the organization. During an incident, such as an information breach, the command-and-control system may find itself in disarray, making it hard to respond promptly and appropriately.

controls.title: Awareness and Compliance with Laws and Guidelines
controls.overview: Applicable laws, standards, and guidelines have been understood and are used to respond to security-related compliance requirements.
controls.status_description: Regularly reviewing laws, regulations, standards, and revised guidelines to ensure compliance, and revising the response policy.
recommended_actions: In addition to IT-related laws, such as the local laws around protection of privacy and personal information, or cybersecurity and unauthorized access, understand requirements and guidelines from regulatory agencies and industry group guidelines for the industry in which your company operates, such as self-regulatory organizations (SRO).
Understand local laws and regulations if your organization is based overseas.

Understand the requirements mandated by laws, or those present under Standards (such as security standards laid out by a government agency, eg NIST in the US, or by industry bodies or professional standards organizations) and establish a response policy to conform to these.
Identify the information assets that are covered by specific requirements and determine how to address the requirements.
Establish a course of action or policies for each requirement, and for requirements that must be met, ensure appropriate compliance.
Regularly check revision to laws and standard or new laws or regulations issued and review the response policy to identify action and maintain compliance.
Periodically confirm compliance with the requirements.
controls.insufficient_measures_risks: If your organization is found non-compliant to applicable laws and standards, it may be the subject of warnings and penalties from regulatory agencies and other government agencies. Occurrence of an incident while your organization is non-compliant, may result in erosion or loss of trust and confidence of society and stakeholders.

controls.title: Establishing and Disseminating the Basic and Overarching Security Policy
controls.overview: The organization's basic overarching security policy has been established and communicated to all applicable workers and users.
controls.status_description: The content of the security policy is regularly reviewed.
recommended_actions: Identify a baseline thinking about protecting information assets from threats and formulate a policy on your organization's stance with respect to security.
Clarify the scope (such as employees, suppliers, sites), on which the security policy applies.
When developing the policy, I obtain approval for that policy document from management.
Notify employees and related external parties of the security policy once established.
Publish the security policy as an external declaration.
Check the effectiveness of policies on a regular basis or when changes in your organization's form of business occur and revise them as needed.

Ensure that the basic overarching security policy is sufficiently realistic to translate into implementable and specific rules and procedures and is not potentially detrimental or disruptive to operations.
controls.insufficient_measures_risks: Without an established and formal security policy, security measures may be inconsistent, and this may result in ad hoc responses, and a consistent security level can not be maintained or improved upon.

controls.title: Establishing and Maintaining Documented Policies and Procedures
controls.overview: Rules and procedures to provide specifics on achieving compliance with the overarching security policy have been developed.
controls.status_description: Documented policies and procedures are regularly reviewed.
recommended_actions: Develop and communicate rules and procedures to provide greater detail on how to achieve compliance or adhere with the overarching security policy.
Obtain management approval on the developed policies, procedures, and rules.
Require employees and relevant external parties to adhere to the established rules and manuals.
Verify that employees/workers and concerned external parties comply with the policies, procedures, and rules.
Review and revise the rules and manuals at least once a year.
Review and revise the rules and procedures addressing internal and external changes such as new laws, regulations, and emerging technologies (e.g., generative AI).
Review and revise the rules and procedures based on audits, training exercises, and incident response outcomes as necessary.
Examples of regulations and manuals:
Information Asset Management Regulations
Risk Assessment Regulations
Risk Assessment Manual
Vulnerability Management Regulations (including content related to diagnosis and testing)
Authentication and Access Management Regulations
Data Management Regulations
Log Management Regulations
External Contractor Management Regulations
System Development Regulations
Physical Security Management Regulations
Network Management Regulations
Incident Response Manual (including recovery procedures)
Security Education Guidelines
Security Drill and Training Guidelines
Etc.
controls.insufficient_measures_risks: Security-related workflows and processes may operate ineffectively, leaving vulnerabilities unaddressed, potentially leading to exploits and actual impact from cyberattacks.

controls.title: Identification and evaluation of security risk
controls.overview: Identify your Organization's cybersecurity and information security risks, with a focus on the nature and form of your business activities, and perform a ascertain and evaluate the impact that these risks may have on the business upon materializing
controls.status_description: Regularly identify and evaluate security risks
recommended_actions: Identifying security risks based on an understanding of your organization's mission
Identify all corporate information and assets (physical, information, intellectual etc., in a wide scope), and assign relative priorities to them based on their business need and importance

Identify critical systems based on internal perspectives (e.g., impact on own organization's mission and business goals) and external perspectives (e.g., impact on customers in case of business interruption)
Identify internal and external security threats (e.g., cyber-attacks and internal fraud)

Identify risks on the downside (i.e. "negative" risks) that could hinder the achievement of your organization's mission and business goals, as well as risks on the upside, (i.e. "positive" risks), or potential, that could provide growth and benefits to your organization
For the assets identified as needing protection from security threats, track the implementation of applicable countermeasures
Evaluate identified security risks
Evaluate the possibility (probability) that a threat will materialize (i.e., actually occur), and the degree of impact when it does This evaluation should be done from all the following methods:
Based on possible scenarios: (e.g. unauthorized access, malware infection, human error, internal fraud)
Based on the “C-I-A” (confidentiality, integrity, availability) rubric
Item-specific (e.g., organization (i.e. teams, departments, function etc.), servers, applications, networks, terminals)
Establish the level and type of risk acceptable to achieve business goals and define risk tolerance in agreement with management
Respond to each security risk (mitigate, accept, avoid, transfer), depending on the impact and risk tolerance
Identify and assess security risks regularly
Regularly (at least once a year) review security and risk assessments based on the latest threat trends

Integrate new perspectives when there are major or wide-ranging changes, such as start of a new business and changes to business model, and perform security risk assessments to identify latest security risks
controls.insufficient_measures_risks: As internal and external factors for an organization change, its business models, importance of any information retained, and security requirements will also change accordingly. However, if existing security measures do not adapt to these changes, the measures will likely become obsolete. Implementation status of security measures and any unaddressed risks cannot be tracked fully anymore. As a result, optimal security measures can no longer be implemented.

controls.title: Planning and management for security risk response
controls.overview: Formulate a response plan for security risks and manage implementation status of countermeasures.
controls.status_description: The plan for implementation of measures is regularly reviewed.
recommended_actions: Prioritize security measures to be implemented using a risk based approach.
Consider the measures to be implemented, based on risk response policy for all identified security risks (mitigate, accept, avoid, transfer).
Consider taking out insurance to cover financial losses caused by a cybersecurity or technology incident.
Perform a cost analysis, such as by comparing the cost required to reduce residual risk against the insurance premium, based on your organization’s current state.
Some insurance companies offer supplementary services, so consider the benefits of these services before purchasing.
Estimate the cost and time required for implementation.
Develop a security risk response plan and manage implementation status.
Establish measurable objectives for the security measures to be implemented (e.g., increase in reporting rate of targeted phishing email training, vulnerability response rate).
Develop a plan that breaks down the measures into phases (implemented in short-term, medium- to long-term, etc.).
Check progress regularly during the planning period.
Establish a process that identifies, assesses, and responds to security risks and obtain management approval.

Regularly report evaluated (quantified) impact of risk(s) and implementation status of security measures to management, translating technical risk factors to show how they may affect the organization’s business.
Perform external audits to check there are no flaws in the security management risk process on a regular basis, or when a significant change occurs.
Review the security risk response plan content.
Regularly (at least once a year) review response plans based on trends in cyber attacks.
After the end of the planning period, evaluate the actions taken as part of the response plan, and measure their effectiveness.
Update countermeasures based on evaluation and audit results.
controls.insufficient_measures_risks: Security risk response plans may not be executed reliably, leading to omissions in countermeasures. Implementation status of security measures and any unaddressed risks cannot be tracked comprehensively; as a result, optimal security measures can no longer be implemented.

controls.title: Leveraging threat intelligence
controls.overview: Collect and analyze cybersecurity information feed and intelligence that supports overall security strategy, security operations, threat detection & response; engage and communicate with stakeholders and concerned parties
controls.status_description: This protocol, as well as the processes for collecting, processing, analyzing, and sharing information, is regularly reviewed
recommended_actions: Establish an overall policy or guiding protocol for the use and leveraging of threat intelligence
Identify the purpose of use and the types of information to be collected; define the overall process to be followed in collection, processing, and analysis of this information
Gather information on emerging threats, alerts, and vulnerabilities from government (or similarly official) sources and security portals
Gather information about cyberattacks (tactics, techniques, procedures, i.e. TTPs) from other organizations via information-sharing forums or communities
Collect logs and alert data from internal security equipment and measures (e.g., firewalls, WAFs, EDRs)
Utilize external resources such as OSINT tools and threat intelligence services
Collect, process, and analyze information according to defined policies and/or protocols, and share with relevant parties as necessary
Analyze collected information to identify potential attack surfaces and determine the need for countermeasures
When conducting cyberattack simulations, use methods employed by threat actors
Use IoC information (e.g., malicious IP addresses, domains) to support prevention, detection, and response to incidents
Providing incident information such as malware infection to public institutions and information sharing forums
Regularly review the process or protocol of collecting, processing, analyzing, and sharing/communication of information
controls.insufficient_measures_risks: The organization may not recognize how its security posture and countermeasures fall short of the prevailing trends in cyber threats; which could result in exploits and actual impact from cyberattacks. Leveraging the knowledge and know-how based on analyses of attack patterns etc. already conducted by other companies can help prevent or control time, cost, and effort in duplicate efforts within your organization.

controls.title: Establishing protocol for proper disclosure and communication of cybersecurity- and information security-related information
controls.overview: Define the stakeholder who should be disclosed a management policy and status of measure against information security risk, and disclose it with an appropriate method
controls.status_description: Content to be disclosed is periodically reviewed
recommended_actions: Voluntarily disclose or share information about security measures, based on predetermined standards regarding (a) the extent or scope of such disclosure, and with (b) who this information should be made available to
Sharing/disclosure should occur in a way that makes the information accessible to the recipient
Disclose the status of response initiatives with respect to security risk factors harmful to the achievement of your organization's mission and goals
If necessary, describe the status of security risk initiatives in information security reports, CSR reports, sustainability reports, securities reports, etc.
Review disclosed content as changes in policies and countermeasures occur
controls.insufficient_measures_risks: Insufficient or inappropriate (or both) disclosure of your organization's handling of cybersecurity risks may lead to a loss of trust from stakeholders in your organization, from the standpoint of responsibility and accountability to the society at large. Your organization's corporate value can significantly decline during incidents.

controls.title: Enforcing cybersecurity- and information security controls across all group companies
controls.overview: Understand the security posture and current state of cybersecurity and information security measures across all group companies, including subsidiaries and affiliated entities; implement countermeasures shared or enforced groupwide
controls.status_description: Regularly grasped the status of the security measures of the entire group and measures
recommended_actions: Periodically evaluate each group company (e.g. full or partial subsidiaries, affiliates, companies part of the same conglomerate etc.), or receive risk assessment and audit results from each company, and understand the status of security countermeasures for the entire group company
Create a checklist to keep track of the status of security measures at each company
Analyze the security measures status for the entire group and take necessary measures to raise the comprehensive security level throughout the group
Set minimum security level that should be protected by all group companies and security level according to the importance of assets handled by each company
Promote improvement of security levels in companies that have not reached the minimum (baseline)security level
Regularly grasp the status of security measures for the entire group and review the required security levels and measures
Update the contents of the checklist to update with changes in the business environment, group structure, and threats
controls.insufficient_measures_risks: Group companies cannot deter incidents such as information breach or fraud, resulting in increased damage to the whole conglomerate and shared brand identity, leading to social credibility loss and falling stock prices.

controls.title: Security assessments before contracting with third parties
controls.overview: Assess security risks before contracting third parties (e.g., commercial partners, vendors, subcontractors)
controls.status_description: Security-related selection criteria for third parties are regularly reviewed
recommended_actions: Define the cybersecurity-/information security-criteria for selecting third parties
Evaluate whether third parties satisfy criteria before establishing formal contractual relationship
Assess potential security risks or vulnerabilities that may arise from engaging with third parties
Assess the level of cybersecurity compliance (as defined within contracts) required of third parties
Review the occurrence of past incidents and how the third party responded, recovered, and implemented recurrence prevention
Use tools such as third-party assessments or security rating services to establish an objective evaluation of risks
Evaluate, for important third parties, their security governance, incident response planning, and contingency planning
Criteria of Regularly reviewed (In addition to criteria of Conducted)
Regularly review these cybersecurity-/information security-criteria, and the means and methods of evaluation
controls.insufficient_measures_risks: The Organization may not recognize how its security posture and countermeasures fall short of the prevailing trends in cyber threats; which could result in exploits and actual impact from cyberattacks. Leveraging the knowledge and know-how based on analyses of attack patterns etc. already conducted by other companies can help prevent or control time, cost, and effort in duplicate efforts within your organization.

controls.title: Specifying security obligations within third party contracts
controls.overview: Delineate and document roles, requirements and delineate scope pertaining to cybersecurity within third-party contracts (e.g., commercial partners, vendors, subcontractors)
controls.status_description: The recorded content is regularly reviewed
recommended_actions: Identify and clarify cybersecurity-/information security-related responsibilities and requirements for both your Organization and the contracting third party
Specify third-party security responsibilities, roles, and requirements in contracts or specifications
Request response and reporting of any serious vulnerabilities discovered during the term of the contract
Request cooperation in developing response and recovery plans and advance preparations (e.g., response drills) in the event of an incident
Request a software bill of materials (SBOM) if a critical product or service vendor maintains a SBOM
Establish provisions for activities that occur after the conclusion of service agreement (e.g., return of information and submission of disposal certificate, revocation of access privileges, etc.)
Request evidence (e.g., self-attestation, conformance to known standards, certifications, or inspections, etc.) of performing acceptable security practices
Establish a contractual right to request audits, and contractual provisions to establish penalties for false disclosures and responses to audit queries
Regularly review the contents of the contract, such as during periodic update or review
controls.insufficient_measures_risks: Ambiguous division of incident response roles and responsibilities may cause delayed or insufficient response, or both.

controls.title: Managing third party security risks
controls.overview: Assess the third party’s (e.g., commercial partners, vendors, subcontractors) cybersecurity posture and readiness against requirements expected by your Organization; require remediation for deficiencies
controls.status_description: Security practices of third parties are regularly reviewed and evaluated
recommended_actions: Identify the role of each third party and maintain an inventory with information on the how important or critical the third party is for your Organization
Identity and track (e.g., in a list) all points-of-contact person or the responsible liaison for security matters
Identity and track (e.g., in a list) all services and functions
Understand the critical data provided to third parties and how it is managed
Establish an overarching security control framework for all third parties and obtain approval from management
Assess the status of security measures of third parties important to your business
Define required or expected security levels corresponding to the third party's degree of importance for the Organization
Request improvement or remediation if the third party's security measures do not meet the required or expected security level
Regularly reassess the importance of third parties and evaluate their security measures on an ongoing basis
Monitor services provided by third parties and detect security events
Continuously monitor legal compliance, service updates, and dark web activity
*Third parties: Business partners, contractors, etc.
controls.insufficient_measures_risks: In outsourcing operations, such as outsourced IT system operations, if the demarcation of responsibilities and management functions between your company and the vendor/contractor is unclear, there is a risk of gaps in coverage, such as during an incident. Incidents within the third-party's organization may bring about secondary impact on your Organization, such as data breaches at the third party involving your Organization's data, or malware spreading from the third party’s to your Organization's.

controls.title: Developing cybersecurity talent
controls.overview: Identify and organize the qualities and skills necessary for the workers involved with information security and impart education or training necessary to acquire them
controls.status_description: Expected competencies, expected skills, and the instructional content/curriculum are regularly reviewed
recommended_actions: Define the roles and required skills and competencies for individuals involved in security-related work and operations; establish policy direction or specific policies to conduct necessary education and training for the individuals to acquire these skills and competencies

Identify professional roles of personnel involved in security operations within your organization (eg, management, strategic management, and practitioners/technicians, etc) and define the qualities and skills that each role should possess
Develop plans to nurture security personnel in the medium / long term, such as establishing a career path or creating an education roadmap
Execute the policy or the roadmap, conducting the education and training stated there
Periodically review the expected competencies, expected skills, and the instructional content/curriculum to keep current with new technologies and emerging threats
Provide security reskilling for personnel not currently involved in security operations, and develop specialized professionals
controls.insufficient_measures_risks: Failure to maintain and improve on an appropriate working experience and professional dealing for workers will prevent your organization from retaining competent cybersecurity personnel.

controls.title: Integrating security throughout workers' and users' lifecycle
controls.overview: Determine the responsibilities and duty related to information security from the beginning of employment of staff to the end of employment, and request the conclusion of the contract and full execution of duties
controls.status_description: Periodic review of responsibilities and obligations is conducted
recommended_actions: Establish responsibilities and obligations surrounding security aspects within the end-to-end human resource lifecycle
Review the background history of candidates, while staying compliant with relevant laws and regulations, and within ethical bounds
Record clauses mandating the responsibilities of an individual employee for cybersecurity on the employment contract
Explain responsibilities and obligations pertaining to cybersecurity to new employees at the time of contract signing (during onboarding process)
Require the signing and submission of a security pledge during onboarding, and keep the pledge on file

Penalties for cases such as security policy violations are specified in employment regulations (eg, in the employee handbook or code of conduct), and disciplinary action is taken when violations occur

Clarify the penalty for disclosing confidential information to a third party with a confidentiality agreement or non-disclosure agreement (NDA) that must be signed and returned by a departing employee at the end of employment, and maintain this commitment as a record
Periodic review of responsibilities and obligations is conducted
controls.insufficient_measures_risks: New employees may not understand their security responsibilities, resulting in an increased security risk to the organization. Failure to sign a valid nondisclosure agreement for a departing employee will increase the possibility of divulging of organization's sensitive information (such as trade secrets) to competitors. No disciplinary action can be taken against workers in violation of security policies or rules. In addition, if the rules and penalties are not made known, security violation cannot be prevented.

controls.title: Security education for employees
controls.overview: Implement necessary information security education or training to general employees not involved directly with information security operation
controls.status_description: Learning expectations and the instructional content/curriculum are regularly reviewed
recommended_actions: Policy direction or specific policies addressing education and training for all employees and workers is established

State and/or establish a code of conduct for employees addressing expectation about knowledge and learning, and clarify timelines to execute the learning plan containing relevant training and learning sessions
Specify conditions that trigger training requirements, such as onboarding or role changes
Provide education and training to employees on topics in cybersecurity/information-security, following the established policy or the roadmap
Often, and on an ongoing basis, share information on the status of occurrence of incidents with employees in order to raise awareness
Prepare specific and easy-to-remember content, such as using the terms of your system or documents
Description of security policies and contingency plans
How to securely manage (store, transfer, destroy, etc) sensitive information
The basic techniques used in cyber attacks and measures for defending against them
How to respond when an incident occurs or is suspected to have occurred
Effectiveness of secure authentication, such as two factor authentication
How to report if you find signs of insider threat/inner crime

Social engineering attack techniques (phishing, tailgating (letting another person in using or together with the authentication of another person), pretext (attacks to steal information by impersonating a trusted person, such as an official or police officer), etc)
How to report a failure to run an automated process tool (such as a configuration management tool or an OS standard automatic updates and patching)
Validate the sufficiency of employees' or workers' understanding, and provide continuous education/training to address insufficiencies
Conduct tests using e-learning (online learning management platforms) and other methods to measure employee understanding of security
Arrange for feedback of education/training results to trained individuals
Review instructional content and the curriculum of education/training at least annually against new trends in technology and cyber threats
Develop and improve the quality of human resource (including from a security standpoint) who can implement necessary and sufficient security measures in the execution of their work
controls.insufficient_measures_risks: The following incidents are likely to occur due to insufficient awareness and skill of officers and employees regarding security. Malware infection from suspicious mails and malicious sites. Internal fraud by retirees and managers (bringing out or sending out of information from company environment, in an unauthorized manner etc.). Information leak due to erroneous transmission of mail.

controls.title: Improving response and readiness to email-based cyberattacks
controls.overview: Training emails that simulate cyber-attacks are sent to executives and employees to assess their ability to respond to cyber-attacks, and countermeasures are implemented based on the results of the training
controls.status_description: The training content is reviewed regularly
recommended_actions: Distribute simulated training, such as targeted phishing emails (spear phishing etc) and fraudulent business email to employees and assess employee preparedness against these attacks
Consider and implement necessary measures, based on the results of the simulation
Implement remedial or supplementary training for users who ended up opening the simulated emails and clicked on attachments and URLs
Consider implementing technical measures such as file extension-based restrictions on attachments and sender domain spoofing countermeasures
Establish a system for reporting and sharing suspicious e-mails
Review the training content and conduct it regularly
Update the simulated exercises based on research and understanding of latest phishing trends; e.g., fine tune the subject line, sender's email address, sender domain etc
controls.insufficient_measures_risks: Awareness and ability to detect phishing attacks among executives and employees, such as targeted emails (spear phishing, whaling) does not improve, resulting in diminished ability to suppress or eliminate incidents such as malware infection due to opening phishing emails.

controls.title: Implementing physical security zoning by asset sensitivity
controls.overview: Establish grades of physical security and zone segregation and divide physical locations into these zones accordingly. Monitor behavior of individuals entering areas classified as sensitive or important in your nomenclature.
controls.status_description: Periodic review of the physical security levels and the scope of locations is conducted
recommended_actions: Define required security levels and classify physical location in these, based on the intended use of the location such as working area and server storage

Physically segregate access environments and locations used to access information assets For example, workspaces are separated according to the attributes, roles, permissions, and kind of information handled, and by who accesses it (employees, partner companies, outsiders) in that space etc.
Physically protect designated locations and equipment (e.g., servers, cabling) from environmental threats (e.g., flooding, fire) and unauthorized access based on their importance
Install surveillance cameras or require escorts in sensitive areas to monitor behavior
Regularly review the security levels used for classification and the range and scope of classification for locations, in response to changes in the layout of working spaces or nature of work
controls.insufficient_measures_risks: Unauthorized persons such as outsiders can easily infiltrate the locations with high importance, causing information leaks and physical theft, etc. Security classifications may not get updated properly with changes in physical layouts, resulting in leak or exposure of information to unintended locations.

controls.title: Implementing physical access and entry control
controls.overview: Use means of authentication of a rigor appropriate to an area's physical security segregation zone or grade to control entry and exit, and obtain and preserve authentication record trail
controls.status_description: The authentication method is reviewed on a regular basis
recommended_actions: Implement appropriate authentication for entering and leaving facilities, based on the security level classification of the location
Safely manage keys and IC cards, and promptly collect or invalidate unnecessary ones
Keep a log of entry and exit records at important facilities and areas

For resources kept under a lock-and-key, retain access records for issuing (granting) the keys, and in the case of IC cards or biometric authentication, keep a log of access records and retain them for a set period
Periodically audit the access records to ensure that there is no unauthorized access
Regularly review lock-and-key management system and authentication methods
controls.insufficient_measures_risks: Unauthorized intrusions, information leaks, and theft may occur in locations of high importance. Further, there is no trace of such fraud and thus it may not be detectable.

controls.title: Physical management of endpoints
controls.overview: Define rules for managing endpoints (PCs, smartphones, tablets, etc.) and confirm that they are appropriately managed
controls.status_description: Rules and solutions, and such, are reviewed regularly
recommended_actions: Set rules to protect terminals from loss or theft and unauthorized access, and inform these rules to employees
Implement clear desk/clear screen policies
Enforce screen lock when leaving one's seat
Wire lock devices (such as portable ones), and put storage locations of terminals under lock and key to prevent loss or theft
Introduce MDM to enable remote data wipe on corporate smartphones or tablets if lost or stolen during their use outside the Organization
Ensure that devices are managed according to rules
Patrol workspaces to visually check implementation status
Use admin distributed settings or similar measures, configure all devices with configuration settings to enforce automatic screen lock after a period of inactivity

Ensure that users notice when communication devices, such as cameras and microphones, are in use, so that they can detect and prevent unauthorized remote operation (by external malicious actors who may have hijacked the devices, etc.)

Regularly review rules and solutions, considering changes in the internal working environment (such as permitting remote work or working from home (WFH), working style reforms in the society as a whole), as well as external environment (such as trends in cyber-attacks)
controls.insufficient_measures_risks: Unauthorized users may access information at an endpoint while the owner is away from the office, causing information leakage or unauthorized operations.

controls.title: Management of information assets
controls.overview: Information assets are managed in accordance with their importance classification, and are maintained and disposed of in adherence to defined and expected procedures
controls.status_description: Information asset management policies and proper asset storage (including retention and archival) and are regularly reviewed
recommended_actions: Define information asset management policies based on their lifecycle (acquisition, use, storage, disposal)

Identify the information assets to be protected and set the level of importance in terms of the degree of impact on internal and external parties in the event of an incident (e.g., data leaks or breaches, falsified data or company branding used wrongfully, etc.)

Define permitted scope of use, retention periods, persons responsible or ownership, and handling methods (storage, disposal, transfer) appropriate to the importance level or sensitivity classification of information assets
Physical information media such as paper and other media, as well as electronic data such as files, should be labeled according to their classification
Permit the use of designated external media only when necessary, and restrict export-capable endpoints

When making information publicly available, such as publishing on the organization's website, etc., establish rules to ensure that the disclosed information does not contain confidential information (e.g., review and approval by multiple people)

Manage information assets following established information asset management policies; maintain a current inventory of assets (e.g., in the form of a list, ledger, database etc.), and include information on the asset's importance level; record activities or interactions with the asset (e.g. when it is viewed, altered, and deleted or disposed)

Store information assets in appropriate locations depending on the type of data (e.g., personally identifiable information, protected health information, financial account numbers, etc.) and include metadata such as storage location and ownership
Restrict access to sensitive data and other important data so that only designated users and systems can access them, and obtain access records
Important external storage media and disks are managed under lock and key, and/or managed under a check-out/check-in system so that they are tracked when they are brought out/returned
Acquire a log related to the use of the external storage device and periodically review it
Periodically delete unnecessary data and data that has passed the protection period stipulated by law, and update the ledger/list in which that data is tracked
For critical information, visualize data flow including contractors
When storing important information (such as personal information), mask the data as necessary
Periodically review the asset management policies; review policy effectiveness in terms of actual compliance
Regularly check for unmanaged personal / confidential information, such as by using a tool
controls.insufficient_measures_risks: Damage from adverse events such as internal fraud, misconduct, or other wrongdoing, or from cyber-attacks can be magnified because important information can be easily removed or tampered with. Inability to meet the requirements (such as those surrounding confidentiality) for "trade secrets" under the Unfair Competition Prevention Law (Japan, or similar requirements elsewhere) and prevent the legal protection of proprietary technologies, knowhow, and other information.

controls.title: Management of hardware assets
controls.overview: Define rules for managing hardware assets (such as PCs, servers, network devices, and smartphones), and manage them appropriately
controls.status_description: Periodically checked inventory of hardware assets
recommended_actions: Define rules for managing hardware assets
Identify hardware assets (including IT, IoT, OT, and mobile devices) to be managed
Ensure that hardware is procured from authorized dealers or reputable distributors
External storage media is restricted to securely managed media approved by the organization
Encrypt the data stored on such external storage media
Collect all leased or provisioned media at the end of the employee's employment
Plan for the discontinuation of hardware reaching the end of its support or lacking necessary security features, and replace and/or dispose of it accordingly

When disposing of storage media, ensure that data has been completely deleted by writing random values on it, deleting encryption keys, physically destroying disks, etc and obtain a disposal (destruction) certificate if necessary
When sending a device for repair or maintenance to a vendor or repair facility etc, ensure that the device does not contain important data
Maintain a list of hardware that should be protected according to rules

Manage configuration information, such as OS and network addresses, and information about hardware assets, such as owner departments and locations, by using IT assets management system or a configuration management system
Monitor networks to detect unauthorized hardware and other unauthorized connections to the network
Use network discovery tools to identify all assets connected to the organization's network
Create and maintain a management ledger (list) to track issue (provisioning or grant) and grants/revocations of removable media
Regularly perform inventories of hardware assets and update the asset inventory as needed
Regularly validate the physical presence and ownership of the hardware asset against its entry within the asset management inventory
Review hardware asset management rules, policies or procedures regularly (at least annually)
Update information about hardware assets periodically or when there is a change to the information, and always ensure it is up to date
*Hardware assets: PCs, servers, network equipment, smartphones, tablets, external storage media, IoT devices, etc.
controls.insufficient_measures_risks: Hardware assets (PC, mobile, external storage media, etc.) that are stolen, lost or taken out in an unauthorized or improper manner cannot be tracked/traced. When unnecessary hardware assets are left unattended on the company network, malware infections may occur in those devices.

controls.title: Management of software assets
controls.overview: Define rules for managing software assets (such as operating systems (OS's) and applications), and maintain their current inventory in lists, or databases; include information about configuration and licenses
controls.status_description: Inventory of software assets is taken periodically
recommended_actions: Define rules for managing software assets
Download software only from authorized vendors or trusted distribution sources

Deploy IT asset management tools (inventory management tools or configuration management systems, ie CMS) to track and maintain configuration information (such as software names, versions, publishers, administrator, installation dates) as well as vendor support information, destination hardware assets, and administrator in a ledger or database
Create a license management ledger (list) etc and manage it to prevent inconsistencies in the number of licenses purchased and the actual need and consumption status
Verify that unauthorized software is not installed
For software not supported by its vendor, record and manage it as an exception
Determine which browsers, mail clients, and versions are permitted to use
Update information about software assets periodically or when there is a change to its information, ensuring that this information is always up to date
controls.insufficient_measures_risks: Vulnerabilities in software installed in your organization environment may not be detected and may be left vulnerable to malware or other threats. Unauthorized use of software, if undetected, cannot be remedied, possibly inviting criminal penalties due to copyright infringement etc. or claims for damages.

controls.title: Managing internal and external information systems
controls.overview: Maintain a current inventory of information systems (including cloud services, and systems managed/owned by individual business units) in lists or databases; include purpose of use and indicate presence or absence of internet exposure
controls.status_description: Inventory of these managed information systems is kept current by reviewing it periodically
recommended_actions: Define internal and external systems (including cloud services) that your organization is responsible for managing
Identify and track all information systems (e.g., business systems) used within your organization
If your organization provides a service or services to customers, identify all systems involved in this activity as such
Define the importance of systems based on internal factors (e.g., business impact) and external factors (e.g., impact on customers during outages)
Identify, track and keep a current inventory of all information systems and external systems used by your organization

Manage identified systems in an inventory/list/ledger with information on managing or owning department, purpose of use, configuration-related information (on-premises/cloud), internet connectivity, FQDN, and IP addresses

Regularly validate the information by auditing the system and its metadata/attributes against its entry within the asset management inventory, and update the inventory information in the list/ledger/database if needed
Regularly search or search the environment for unmanaged or unrecognized systems to maintain inventory accuracy and completeness
Regularly review the criteria for defining system criticality and the criticality assigned to each system
controls.insufficient_measures_risks: Neglecting information assets' security measures may lead to potential exploits and actual damage.

controls.title: Understand network configuration
controls.overview: Create a network diagram of your company and grasp all communications and data related to company's business
controls.status_description: Whether or not there are discrepancies between the actual situation and the configuration chart is periodically checked
recommended_actions: Create a diagram showing connections between network devices and systems (this could be variably referred to as a network diagram, a network configuration diagram, a network configuration state and flow diagram)
Understand all business-related communications and data flows between users and systems
For each network device or equipment, manage a record of its configuration rules, such as permitted communication (inbound/outbound), and the business justification to support or justify this
Regularly check that there is no difference between the configuration diagram (mentioned above) and the actual device configuration or data flow
controls.insufficient_measures_risks: If the network configuration is not well understood, unexpected misconfiguration or unauthorized changes can lead to unauthorized or improper access to information from outside the organization.

controls.title: Standardizing secure configuration sets for servers, and server hardening
controls.overview: Manage the hardware and software items and versions which comprise systems and services
controls.status_description: Configuration information is regularly reviewed and kept current
recommended_actions: Understand all component hardware and related software (including virtual OSes or cloud components) that comprise the wider system; record this information (configuration) in a listing or inventory database, along with version number etc. of each component
Associate Active Ports, Services, and Protocols with an asset inventory/list/database/ledger
Use DHCP logging or IP address management tools to identify assets connected to the system
Establish a baseline secure configuration standard based on the principle of least privilege (PoLP)
Periodically apply system configuration settings automatically using a system settings management tool to prevent unintentional changes to configuration settings
Check if the configuration settings have been changed to unauthorized settings, or verify that no unauthorized service is running
Confirm that system software has not been tampered with by secure boot, TPM, verification of digital signature, etc.
Uninstall or disable unnecessary services, such as unused file sharing services, web application modules, and service features
Periodically confirm that system configuration information is up to date
controls.insufficient_measures_risks: It is difficult to determine whether the discovered vulnerability will affect your organization's systems, potentially leading to unauthorized access and malware infection.

controls.title: Standardizing secure configuration sets for endpoints, and endpoint hardening
controls.overview: Standardize security settings configuration, such as hardening baselines, for endpoints (PC, smartphone, tablet, etc.)
controls.status_description: Security settings are reviewed periodically
recommended_actions: Establish standards for secure settings/configurations, such as proper setting values and minimum required software
Disable unauthorized plugins and restrict use of scripting languages in web browsers and email clients
Use digital signatures, version control, etc. to restrict execution to only approved scripts
Prevent automatic execution of external storage media

Enable built-in exploit prevention functionalities of operating systems (Microsoft ® Data Execution Prevention (DEP), Windows ® Defender Exploit Guard (WDEG), Apple ® System Integrity Protection (SIP), Gatekeeper, Address Space Layout Randomization (ASLR), and others)
Enable Command Line Audit Logging
Uninstall or disable unnecessary services, such as unused file sharing services, web application modules, and service features
Define and configure the DNS servers your enterprise uses
Distribute secure checklist of standard settings and perform uniform kitting with standard settings (i.e. to a standard configuration set up)
Verify that secure setting is maintained over time
Regularly review secure settings of all devices and equipment, in line with the latest technological trends and convenience
controls.insufficient_measures_risks: If the security configuration of devices is not standardized and vulnerable configurations remain, there is a risk of unauthorized access and malware infection.

controls.title: Restriction of unauthorized software
controls.overview: Restrict the installation and execution of unauthorized software on the endpoints (PC, smartphone, tablet, etc.)
controls.status_description: Software subject to approval or otherwise is regularly reviewed
recommended_actions: Define the set of software that is permitted or not, based on the needs of the business
Define a process for permitting unauthorized software (not present in the set above) as an exception
Restrict installation and execution of unauthorized software
Confirm that unauthorized software is not installed or executed on client terminals, and uninstall or stop the execution if any is found
To ensure that only authorized software can be installed, IT infrastructure manager controls the endpoint privilege such as not giving users administrator permission on the client terminals
Leverage restrictions such as AppLocker (Windows feature) to allow only authorized software
Review software regularly that you allow or disallow
*Endpoints: PCs, smartphones, tablets, etc.
controls.insufficient_measures_risks: Infection with malware by installing or running software from suspicious emails and unauthorized web sites is more likely to occur.

controls.title: Understand network configuration
controls.overview: Manage the version of network devices and install the latest stable version when updates are available
controls.status_description: Periodic information updated is confirmed and the scope of management is reviewed
recommended_actions: Identify network devices (firewall, router, switch, etc.) that should be subject to the organization's administration
Managing a list/database/ledger of network devices including version information
Track the versions of network devices and install the latest stable version when updates become available
Establish and apply a set of or standard for secure settings/configurations, standards, e.g. not exposing internal ports to the Internet, prohibiting communication between unnecessary servers
When using an IP phone (VoIP), control and monitor it to prevent eavesdropping, spoofing, and unauthorized use by a third party
Manage network devices and their versions using infrastructure-as-code (IaC)
Confirm that the information related to network devices is up-to-date and regularly review management targets
Automatically check or scan for unidentified assets using tools such as attack surface management tools
controls.insufficient_measures_risks: Proper treatment of vulnerabilities may not be possible, leaving dangerous vulnerability untreated, and possibly leading to defects or operational malfunctions.

controls.title: Vulnerability management process
controls.overview: Establish a process for identifying, assessing and dealing with vulnerabilities of systems or applications
controls.status_description: Information sources, as well as the evaluation criteria for vulnerability application, are all reviewed on a regular basis
recommended_actions: Promptly address critical vulnerabilities when identified
Develop vulnerability management process (information collection, information evaluation, patch application, etc.)
Create a list of sources (sites or vendors) to collect vulnerability information
Identify vulnerabilities in your organization's assets from gathered vulnerability information

If your organization provides services, establish a process for responding to and processing reports of vulnerabilities related to the services from external parties (such as customers, subcontractors, or government agencies)
Check the importance of the system, the content of the vulnerability and the prescribed patch application criteria and consider the response policy
Before applying a patch, follow a predefined procedure to verify it in a test environment and prepare a procedure for removing the patch in the event of an error
If a decision is made for some vulnerabilities to not be patched, appropriate risk reduction measures should be taken
Centralized management of patch status
Deploy a tool to automatically install updates provided by software vendors for operating systems and other software, and confirm that such updates are properly applied
Review information sources and regularly review the criteria for applying patches
controls.insufficient_measures_risks: Proper response to vulnerabilities cannot be implemented, and dangerous vulnerability persists, making the device/software etc. susceptible to malware. When a patch is applied without sufficient testing of its operation in a test environment or the like, unexpected system suspensions, or operational malfunctions are likely to occur.

controls.title: Conducting penetration tests
controls.overview: Conduct penetration testing
controls.status_description: Perspectives of penetration tests are regularly reviewed in order that recent threats can be countered
recommended_actions: Perform penetration tests on system infrastructure applications and plan response based on test results
Penetration tests should be conducted with the consent of relevant parties in accordance with a predetermined plan to minimize the impact on operations
Create a test environment for penetration testing as needed
Properly manage the accounts used for penetration testing by deleting them after the test is complete
Request a penetration test from a professional organization with specialized skills and experience
Determine the frequency and timing of the penetration test, and execute it as specified
Regularly review the considerations (aims, methodology, items to be tested and their relative importance etc.) of penetration testing to combat the latest attack methods and threats
Implement corrective actions based on the findings of the penetration test
controls.insufficient_measures_risks: Vulnerabilities could persist within the system, and they can be exploited to gain unauthorized access from outside.

controls.title: Creating and provisioning access and accounts, and conducting access inventory
controls.overview: Set a process for account management and manage it according to the processes you have established
controls.status_description: Accounts are reviewed periodically through an inventory process
recommended_actions: Issue accounts adhering to the established protocol, policy, or procedure governing new accounts issuing or provision
Issue accounts in line with security requirement level (privileged access, high-level access, general access, etc)
Abolish use of shared ID as much as possible and manage all access through individual accounts (ie accounts per individual)
Set an expiration date for all issued accounts, at the time of issuing
To uniquely identify the user, reuse of the same ID is restricted for a certain period after the account ID is destroyed

Promptly delete or disable accounts following the user's (employee, etc.) HR transfer (e.g., of roles/departments etc.) or separation (resignation, termination, etc.), such as over a sync with the connected HRM, or other source of truth
Automatically disable or remove accounts that are not used for a period
To maintain an audit trail, when deleting an account, deactivate the account for a period before fully deleting the account
Maintain a list of user accounts and periodically perform inventory of accounts
Conduct account inventory regularly (at least once every quarter)
controls.insufficient_measures_risks: A high privilege account, that can access important information, may be created without approval, potentially leading to information leaks.

controls.title: Authenticating accounts
controls.overview: Authenticate users by using appropriate method when they access to the system used for business purposes
controls.status_description: The authentication method is reviewed on a regular basis
recommended_actions: Authenticate users when accessing systems
Notify the administrator when an account with "general" level access fails login multiple times, or automatically lock the account
Notify the administrator when the login of the administrator account fails, and automatically lock the account when it fails multiple times
During password authentication, mask the entered password with asterisks, etc.

Choose an authentication method appropriate for the security risk associated with a business activity or type of business operation related to that system (eg implementation of biometric authentication, multifactor authentication)
Understand and track the authentication system used for each system
Restrict authentication systems to as few as possible by integrating and centralizing authentication and managing all account access level settings (eg by way of Active Directory implementation)

When implementing Single Sign-On, define and implement authentication protocols and methods in conformance to guidelines and best practices for the respective authentication protocols (SAML 20, OAuth 20, OpenID Connect, JWT (JSON Web Token)) used, to ensure that identity assertions are properly generated, protected, and verified
Review the authentication method regularly
Review your organization's authentication methods and their (technical) implementations by checking for issuance and updates of related guidelines
controls.insufficient_measures_risks: Information leakage due to "unauthorized access to information that is not permitted to use" cannot be prevented.

controls.title: Managing access privilege
controls.overview: Establish policy to assign account access privilege and manage access privilege
controls.status_description: It is periodically checked that access privileges have been allotted correctly
recommended_actions: Assign access privileges to an account following the defined access rights assignment process
Allow or restrict access to each piece of information and to each system, matching with the access privilege
Establish access control policies and allocation processes based on the principle of least privilege (PoLP) and separation of duties (SoD), also called segregation of duties

Ensure that access privileges of employees' accounts are updated immediately in response to events such as separation (termination) of employment relationship or transfer, such as by integrating with the HR database or people administration system; employment events could include all workers in general, and transfer could include transfer of roles, teams, or other human resource transfer
Regularly conduct inventory and review of access privilege (i.e. periodic audit)
Conduct an inventory of access privileges regularly (at least once every quarter)
controls.insufficient_measures_risks: Accounts not intended to access that information may be able to access it, or accounts dormant or unused for a long time or obsolete accounts may continue to access accounts, potentially leading to information leaks.

controls.title: Establishing and adopting password policies
controls.overview: Establish and adopt the password strength required for each system and the frequency to be updated
controls.status_description: The password policy is regularly reviewed
recommended_actions: Set a password policy
When notifying the password to the user, establish rules such as verifying the recipient's identity
Ensure that the initial temporary password issued and communicated to the user is changed
Always change default password present in new systems ("factory reset" versions of password must be changed before putting in use)
Disallow the use of the same password for some iterations of password changes (password history)
Use a different password for each system
Require a password whose strength is in accordance with the security requirement level (privileged access, high-level access, general access, etc.)
Set the password strength higher if multi-factor authentication is not available for highly privileged accounts, such as administrator accounts
Systematically controlled in accordance with an established policy, or the policy is thoroughly complied with
Regularly review password policies
controls.insufficient_measures_risks: Accepting weak passwords increases the possibility of system unauthorized access due to password cracking.

controls.title: Monitoring and responding to unusual access
controls.overview: Monitor unusual account usage, such as logging in other than business hours, and take corrective action such as account suspension if necessary
controls.status_description: The definition of normal and abnormal account behavior is reviewed periodically
recommended_actions: Define what could be unusual behavior for accounts, and periodically check account usage status
Notify the administrator when an account under their control has an unusually long log-in session, or has a log in outside of normal business hours, and subject this account to audit
Monitor account behavior in real-time, and suspend accounts as necessary
Forcibly log off or disconnect an account after a period of inactivity
Detect login attempts to disabled accounts
Use behavior analytics software (eg, UEBA) to detect anomalous or suspicious user activity to mitigate insider threats
Periodically review the definitions of what constitutes unusual account behaviors
controls.insufficient_measures_risks: Cyber-attacks and unauthorized or improper activity within the organization may go undetected, leading to potential data leaks.

controls.title: Implementing a process governing the use of privileged accounts
controls.overview: Maintain the processes of application and approval of privileged account
controls.status_description: Regularly monitor and reviewed process
recommended_actions: Issue individual accounts (ie accounts provisioned to a person or access assigned to individual user accounts, versus a group address or shared permissions) for privileged access to operators who perform privileged work
Enforce multi-factor authentication for privileged accounts
Issue accounts for privileged access through the application/approval process, and store and manage record of this issue
Manage privileged accounts in list/ledger/central database etc.
Clarify how user roles are defined for each business application
Confirm that accounts with privileged are properly managed and regularly review the application/approval process
Regularly review privileged account assignments
controls.insufficient_measures_risks: Deficient management of disallowed access pathways, and outside of the organization's tracking and management of accounts, can result in actions being taken on these systems with these accounts.

controls.title: Prior approval for privileged access, and reconciling activity logs against approved scope
controls.overview: Require raising prior approval before use of privileged access and accounts; subsequently, reconcile activity and/or access logs against the scope of use authorized in the approved prior request
controls.status_description: The work check/comparison process itself is being reviewed
recommended_actions: Enable identification of privileged workers (or privileged access users)
Abolish use of shared ID as much as possible and manage all access through individual accounts (ie accounts per individual)
If sharing privileged accounts, use just-in-time (JIT) access that involves provisioning access each time it is required, and maintain records of this process
After completing production environment operations, check the contents of the request for access against the actual operation log to verify that there is no unauthorized operation
Implement a process of requesting and approving privileged operations in advance
Perform operations following predefined steps
Acquire the operation record such as command log and GUI videos
Execute production environment operations under the presence of multiple people
Acquire Access/Create/Edit/Delete log to production data and Log data retrieval from the production environment
To enable privileged work to be performed by remote access, define and control the workers and tasks allowed/necessary for this activity
Confirm privileged work content and review the match process itself to improve efficiency
controls.insufficient_measures_risks: Without appropriate oversight, control, and logging, when fraudulent activity using a privileged ID occurs, it may not be possible to detect it. Without appropriate tracking and record keeping of the operation, it may not be possible to investigate the operation ex post facto and insufficient information to perform an adequate investigation.

controls.title: Encryption of data in transit
controls.overview: Encrypt outgoing information and communication data.
controls.status_description: There is a regular check to see whether the encryption method has been compromised or not
recommended_actions: Identify and list the communication data (ie data in transit) that should be encrypted, and establish policies such as encryption procedure
Only use encryption methods (algorithms, protocols etc) that have been verified and certified for use in encryption of data in transit
Encrypt data communication and network traffic in accordance with defined policies
Encrypt data when sending externally via email or cloud storage
Encrypt communication for publicly exposed systems (e.g., by enforcing HTTPS)
Encrypt account names and authentication information when sent over a network
Encrypt communication in remote access connections
Encrypt confidential information or backup files when transferring or forwarding
Use encrypted communication for all control communication, such as communication for network device management
Encrypt wireless communication with AES etc
Regularly check if an encryption algorithm in use is reported as compromised
controls.insufficient_measures_risks: There is a risk of cyber-attacks, such as eavesdropping on and tampering with communications.

controls.title: Encryption of data at rest
controls.overview: Encrypt data which is stored in the endpoints and servers
controls.status_description: There is a regular check to see whether the encryption method has been compromised or not
recommended_actions: Identify and list the data at rest that should be encrypted, and establish policies such as encryption procedures
Only use encryption methods (algorithms, protocols etc) that have been verified and certified for use in encryption of data at rest
Encrypt stored data (i.e., data at rest) in accordance with defined policies
Encrypt hard disks etc (storage) of devices, equipment, or servers
Encrypt data stored in external storage media
Encrypt backup data
Hash and salt (cryptographic salting) the stored authentication information
Implementing IRM / DRM (Information Rights Management, and Digital Rights Management) as necessary, to encrypt files, restrict reading and writing, and record operation history
Implementing DLP (Data Loss Prevention) as necessary and carry out detection and use restrictions when data is taken out of control range
Regularly check if an encryption algorithm in use is reported as compromised
controls.insufficient_measures_risks: Important information in an unencrypted (plain text, etc.) state is readily available to read and extract, and results in information leaks. Leaked information cannot be deleted afterwards.

controls.title: Acquiring and protecting backups
controls.overview: Obtain and protect backups of important data and perform restore tests
controls.status_description: A restore test is periodically conducted
recommended_actions: Acquire backups and protect the obtained backup data
Identify important information (including file servers and database servers) that should be backed up
Protect backup data securely using methods such as physical security or encryption
Store the backup data at a remote location, geographically removed from the location of the system where the backup was acquired
Develop a process to recover data from backups
Define the/a backup frequency based on the importance of the data and take backup periodically
Retain and manage backup versions to have multiple choices of restore points in the past
Regularly check that important information is backed up and periodically carry out recovery testing
Review and modify as appropriate, the process of recovering data from backups
controls.insufficient_measures_risks: If the information is encrypted, altered or deleted due to malware infection (including Ransomware), the data may not be recovered.

controls.title: Protecting endpoints and servers from malware
controls.overview: Install malware detection products on endpoints and network devices
controls.status_description: Signature files/databases and the behavior engines are regularly updated
recommended_actions: Malware infection is detected by matching malware pattern (signature-based detection) files, a type of knowledge-based detection
Deploy signature-based anti-malware software on network devices, servers, and endpoints
Configure these systems to automatically scan for malware by matching pattern files (signatures) when inserting or connecting external storage media
Monitor detection status involving matching malware with pattern file (signature definitions file)
Regularly update the scanning software and pattern files (signature definitions file)
Always check for pattern file updates and apply them immediately
Malware infection is detected by employing behavior-based anti-malware software
Deploy behavior-based anti-malware software on network devices, servers, and endpoints
Configure these systems to automatically scan for malware by matching pattern files when inserting or connecting external storage media
Monitor detection status from the use of a behavior-based anti-malware software
Regularly update scanning software and behavior profiles (behavior definitions)
Regularly review malware detection methods and means for effectiveness
Centrally manage anti-malware software and regularly check its usage
controls.insufficient_measures_risks: If the signature file, with the latest training based on known attack patterns, is not updated, latest malware cannot be detected or blocked. Infection by unknown malware may not be prevented.

controls.title: Implementation of endpoint log collection and immediate response to malware infection (e.g. EDR product/solution)
controls.overview: Implement products to acquire endpoint logs, to actively detect threats, to visualize suspicious behavior and respond in real time when malware infection occurs (e.g. EDR solution)
controls.status_description: The details and methodology of the response are reviewed on a regular basis
recommended_actions: Implement logging at endpoints with a granularity and level of detail sufficient for tracking malicious programs, when a malware infection is detected and must be tracked (examples of actions to be logged: read or write out (print) operations on files, operations on the OS registry, processes started, access to networks etc.)
Obtain command-line audit logs (such as PowerShell or BASH) for the device, equipment, or other machines applicable
Implement mechanisms to prevent or preempt operations by malware (malicious or unauthorized communication, unauthorized encrypted communication, executing malicious programs, etc.)
Implement mechanisms to automatically restore the machine and its state to their proper state, such as by deleting unauthorized programs)
Regularly simulate logging status, and timely and swift response to malware infection on devices
controls.insufficient_measures_risks: Malware infection may not be prevented. In the event of an actual malware infection, it might be hard to detect and stop the spread of infection in a timely and swift manner.

controls.title: Network segmentation
controls.overview: Enforce network segmentation that is appropriate to your organization’s structuring and operations
controls.status_description: The Organization network is regularly reviewed to validate that segmentation is operating as expected, and as stated in the design
recommended_actions: Prepare the segmentation design of your network so that it is appropriate to your organization’s structuring and business operations
Design segments to allow the minimum two-way communication required
Segregate the data plane (communication traffic) from the control plane
Demarcate segments at the level of business unit (organization unit, department, etc.)

Design segments by assuming that malicious actors have gained capability of lateral movement (that involve attackers or malware spread across the breadth of the internal network), so that such segments allow containment and protection during an actual intrusion
Roll out the actual physical/logical network segmentation, based on the designed network architecture
Perform network management operations in an isolated environment or device separate from the main network
Based on risk and operational management load, implement host-level segmentation or micro-segmentation as needed
Ensure that only authorized systems can communicate across isolated network segments
Regularly review and monitor the operating status and effectiveness of network segmentation, and adjust or improve as needed
controls.insufficient_measures_risks: Unintended actors, or users/actors not originally intended to have access, may be able to access information. In an unsegregated environment, malware infection can spread across the organizations via the network, to other devices and departments.

controls.title: Denying communication which is not permitted
controls.overview: Block connection from unauthorized IP address or port to internal and/or external network
controls.status_description: The definitions of unauthorized communication are reviewed on a regular basis
recommended_actions: Block communication over unauthorized IP addresses or ports
Define and duly restrict disallowed communication after implementing network segmentation (e.g., using on-premises or cloud-based firewalls)
Deny traffic over disallowed or blocked TCP or UDP ports
Between VLANs, allow only authorized systems to communicate only with other systems specifically identified as such, and this should be limited to an individually identified business operation
Implement and manage virtual firewalls and OS firewalls on servers
Use a whitelist approach for firewall settings, in which only expressly allowed and necessary communication is permitted (for allow/deny rules)
If you use the blocklist method, collect threat information as appropriate and add it to the rules
Ensure unauthorized communications are properly restricted
Regularly scan devices deployed in your network, such as hardware firewalls, using vulnerability scanners
Implement mechanisms to compare all network equipment settings and to receive (and not miss) notifications when a deviation is found
Record network packets that cross the boundary
Regularly review the definition of communication to be rejected
controls.insufficient_measures_risks: Internal systems may be exposed to threats from the public internet, and malicious access.

controls.title: Detection of unauthorized communication from outside
controls.overview: Detect the unauthorized communication from outside and block it if necessary
controls.status_description: The detection trend is analyzed, and the definitions for fraudulent communication as well as methods for coping with it are reviewed on a regular basis
